newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended slightly higher Thursday amid moderate volumes but the complex was struggling to resume its month-long rally after last week's correction, traders said.
"The precious metals complex has seen a steadier tone of late, and was probably helped today by the slump in stock and bond prices," Merrill Lynch commodities research director, Bill O'Neill said.
"Some new shorts have entered the market as the recovery waned, and we've seen some producer hedging this week, but support is holding for now," he said.
COMEX April gold closed up $1.30 an ounce at $354.40, after again finding support around $352.00. COMEX gold total estimated volume was 38,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $353.10/60, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $352.90 and the New York close Wednesday around $351.80/30.

But COMEX gold open interest rose Wednesday by 2,477 lots to 173,309 lots, suggesting some funds may be selling short again, but open interest is still well off the peak of 206,584 contracts seen during last year's slide to three year lows.

Swiss commercial banks were seen heavy buyers of put options this week, after last week's announcement by the Swiss government of a plan to sell some gold reserves over a 10 year period to fund a Holocaust's victims fund.
Last year the Swiss also announced a proposal to change the constitutional requirement mandating gold reserves be held against 40 percent of the Swiss francs on issue.

"The melting down of the great glacier of central bank gold holdings is proceeding at a much faster pace now than before the Swiss announcements were made," Merrill Lynch metals analyst Ted Arnold said.

But in the short term implied gold lease rates drifted even lower Thursday, with the one month rate falling below 1.00 percent, suggesting there was little speculative shorting activity, traders said.
And Indian wedding season demand was providing some support for bullion prices in the Far East, analysts said.
COMEX May silver ended up 8.5 cents at $5.305, after again finding some resistance around $5.300.

Open interest in COMEX silver fell a further 203 lots Wednesday to 88,816 contracts, suggesting long's may be taking profits on the breakout in February from a year long downtrend. Silver open interest has fallen from a high of 100,688 lots on February 20.
NYMEX April platinum ended up $2.10 at $386.00 an ounce, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread steady around $31.60 an ounce.
NYMEX June palladium closed up $1.60 at $156.00 an ounce.

In overnight news, Alexander Kulikov, the deputy chief executive of Russia's metal export agency, Almaz, confirmed Wednesday's report that it was possible Russian export's of platinum group metals to Japan may resume at the end of March or in early April.
Annual supply contract talks between the Russians and Japanese broke down last December.
But most analysts still see Russian exports falling in 1997, while demand for palladium for automotive emission catalysts is seen rising, especially in the U.S.
-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641.
